# DOCX validation fixtures

All documents are synthetic. No student material, personal document or sealed evaluation content is included.

- `word-basic-v1.docx` and `word-basic-v2.docx` derive from files saved by Microsoft Word 16.78 on macOS. Only `docProps/core.xml` author and last-editor metadata were scrubbed and the ZIP repacked. `word/document.xml` bytes are identical to the corresponding original Word save. The `.txt` files are exact expected extraction, without a final newline.
- `zip-unicode-path-alias.docx` is an independent reviewer's synthetic adversarial ZIP. Its Info-ZIP Unicode Path extra field tries to replace `harmless.xml` with `word/document.xml`. It must be rejected as Unsupported before the ZIP library resolves that alias.
- `word-layout-v1.docx` and `word-layout-v2.docx` preserve the **original Word ZIP layout**, including growth hints, offsets, flags, sizes and every other entry's exact bytes. Only core.xml's compressed payload and its local/central CRCs changed. `scrub_word_fixture.py` makes equal-byte-length author replacements and searches for exactly the original compressed length; it never repacks. `word-layout.json` records original/fixture hashes and the only allowed changed ranges. An independent byte comparison confirmed zero differences outside those ranges.
- `nested-eocd.docx` and its control reproduce the central-directory disagreement identified by A: zip 8.6.0 selects `FAKE BODY` from the commented variant, while the normal directory describes `REAL BODY`. docx-1 accepted it; docx-2 refuses archive comments with no text. The test asserts the library's different body selection before checking rejection.
- `aes-method-override.docx` has method-0 outer headers but AES extra 0x9901 tells zip to use Deflate. docx-1 accepted it; docx-2 explicitly refuses AES metadata. The test checks the actual library method so it cannot pass merely because of an unrelated limit.
- `validation.json` records current docx-2 Word-layout, immutable Snapshot, regression and performance runs. Historical docx-1 measurements remain in `validation-docx1.json`, explicitly superseded. Original Word bytes and test app-data are local at `/private/tmp/traeva-docx-word-66/`.
- `r2-review.json` records independent **development** review of the frozen docx-2 Reader and the earlier 78-test suite. The earlier `independent-review.json` is marked superseded because A found real defects. `rich-review.json` separately records the incremental 79-test fixture/helper review. These reports are not Codex-R acceptance or the 10/13 Go decision.

Fixture sources: the D-created Word document contains only a title, blank paragraph, Chinese/Latin text, emoji, a tab and two lines. The second save changes `Beta` to `Beta revised`. No macros, remote resources or model calls are used.

`rich-source.docx` is the generated synthetic input, with expected supported text in `rich-source.txt`. The expected text intentionally ends in one space after `Revision anchor`, without a final LF: that space is present in the supported stored text and must not be trimmed. It covers header PAGE, list, table, SEQ field, footnote, comment and tracked revisions. `rich-source-validation.json` records the generated-input run separately.

`word-rich.docx` derives from an actual Microsoft Word 16.78 GUI Save As of that input under the #65 UI slot. Word retained all eight checked features, converting the body SEQ field from complex controls to `fldSimple`. Extraction matches all 108 expected Unicode scalars and returns Partial with six actual omission categories. `word-rich-validation.json` records the original/fixture hashes, exact allowed byte ranges, feature checks, retained validation failures, timings and real immutable Snapshot read after the synthetic source was renamed and the service reopened in a new process. The original saved file remains local at `/private/tmp/traeva-docx-word-66/r2-rich/word-rich-renamed.docx`.

The rich fixture also preserves the actual Word ZIP layout: only core.xml's compressed payload and two CRC fields changed. Its original packed length required a valid intermediate Deflate sync flush; no trailing bytes or repacking were used. The helper checks decompression identity and all byte changes. Its fallback leaves the basic v1/v2 fixture bytes unchanged. This is limited stored-text/omission validation, not a full Word lifecycle or Semantic Change/Retrieval acceptance run.

`word-lifecycle-validation.json` records the follow-up on main `6cc3a60`: two approved Reader note fixes, 84 Reader/Snapshot tests, actual Word 16.78 ordinary/no-change/successive saves and immutable Snapshot reads after rename/move/process restart. It explicitly retains the uncaptured v3 and FileChanged replacement boundary; it does not claim production Word Memory acceptance. Newly saved Word packages and expected body files stay local, while this JSON publishes only hashes, statuses and metadata. `lifecycle-development-review.json` describes the separate developer review, not R1 acceptance. See [the lifecycle report](../../../../../docs/features/docx-word-lifecycle.md) for reproduction and evidence scope.
